messages.subject: Renjin and forecast package.
parts:
Hello everyone.

I'm trying to use R for time series forecasting. I've found that there's a package for Renjin here : http://packages.renjin.org/packages/forecast.html
I've added all dependencies :

            <dependency>
                <groupId>org.renjin</groupId>
                <artifactId>renjin-script-engine</artifactId>
                <version>0.7.0-RC7-SNAPSHOT</version>
            </dependency>

            <dependency>
                <groupId>org.renjin.cran</groupId>
                <artifactId>forecast</artifactId>
                <version>4.04-SNAPSHOT</version>
            </dependency> 

Then I ran simple test:

public class SampleScript {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        // create a script engine manager
        ScriptEngineManager factory = new ScriptEngineManager();
        // create a Renjin engine
        ScriptEngine engine = factory.getEngineByName("Renjin");
        // evaluate R code from String
        Object obj = engine.eval("library(forecast)");
    }
}

And got this exception: org.renjin.eval.EvalException: colorspace could not be found
It seems like forecast library depends on colorspace which is not supported yet.

Then I've decided to look into forecast package contents and there was just one class, which those methods: 

    public static void update(org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p1, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p2, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p3, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p4, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p5, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p6, int p7, int p8, int p9, double p10, double p11, double p12, double p13, double p14) { /* compiled code */ }

    public static void forecast(double p1, double p2, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p3, int p4, int p5, int p6, double p7, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p8, int p9) { /* compiled code */ }

    public static void etsforecast(org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p1, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.IntPtr p2, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.IntPtr p3, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.IntPtr p4, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p5, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.IntPtr p6, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p7) { /* compiled code */ }

    public static void etssimulate(org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p1, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.IntPtr p2, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.IntPtr p3, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.IntPtr p4, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.IntPtr p5, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p6, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p7, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p8, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p9, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.IntPtr p10, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p11, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p12) { /* compiled code */ }

    public static void etscalc(org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p1, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.IntPtr p2, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p3, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.IntPtr p4, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.IntPtr p5, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.IntPtr p6, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.IntPtr p7, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p8, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p9, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p10, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p11, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p12, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p13, org.renjin.gcc.runtime.DoublePtr p14) { /* compiled code */ }

So I think I could use some of those to actually do the forecast, but couldn't find any documentation on parameters. So is there any documentations on them or can I just use forecast lib wthout drawing plots somehow?

Thanks in advance.

messages.author: f06db63329fab1f9
messages.subject: Re: Renjin and forecast package.
parts:
Hi there,

It looks like the forecast package "Depends" on colorspace, so it will fail when loading unfortunately. 

The java methods that you're looking at are just the C/Fortran components of the forecast package and will likely not be much use. The R code is serialized in AST form as a resource, and is evaluated at runtime. 

Unfortunatley time for Renjin has a bit short in December due to other projects, but I think that the next release should solve this problem. If you don't mind getting your hands dirty in the meantime, I can suggest checking out Renjin from master, and setting up a maven build for the forecast package in the same format that you see the stats package in Renjin's repo (https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/tree/master/packages/stats) and remove the bits that depend on colorspace. 

More time for Renjin and the next release is coming in the new year!

Best,
Alex
